companies.notes: LG Energy Solution Holland, Michigan — long-running facility (since ~2012) that underwent a $1.7B expansion. The expansion pivoted from NMC EV pouch cells to LFP ESS cells. New LFP plant opened May 2025 with 3 lines (2 active, 1 by end 2025/early 2026). Current capacity: ~17 GWh LFP ESS. Target 30 GWh by end 2026.

research.summary: LG Energy Solution's Holland, Michigan plant launched its new LFP battery production in May 2025, pivoting from the originally planned EV NMC pouch cells to LFP cells exclusively for grid-scale energy storage. The facility reached ~17 GWh annual capacity by end 2025 with plans to expand to 30 GWh by end 2026. LGES announced this expansion on its Q2 2025 earnings call.

research.summary: GM sold its stake in the Lansing, Michigan Ultium Cells Plant 3 to LG Energy Solution in Q1 2025. LG then partnered with Toyota to supply high-nickel NCMA battery modules from this facility for Toyota's US EV models. The 41 GWh plant is nearly complete and entered production in late 2025. This represents a significant ownership restructuring from the original GM-LG JV model.

companies.notes: Amprius Technologies' Brighton, Colorado gigafactory — 775,000 sq ft silicon anode cylindrical cell plant on a 103-acre site, funded in part by a $50M DOE grant. Phase 1 targets 500 MWh; full scale 5 GWh. Production start moved from 2025 to mid-2026. Amprius took a $22.5M asset impairment charge in Q4 2025 related to the Colorado facility, raising concerns about the timeline. Current revenue comes from external Korean manufacturing capacity (~1.8 GWh).

research.summary: Amprius Technologies selected a 775,000 sq ft site in Brighton, CO for a silicon anode lithium-ion battery gigafactory targeting 5 GWh at full scale. Phase 1 (~500 MWh) was slated for mid-2026, but the company took a $22.5M asset impairment charge linked to the Colorado facility in Q4 2025, suggesting construction complications or timeline changes. Amprius reported strong revenue growth ($28.5M in Q1 2026, +150% YoY) but continues to rely on South Korean manufacturing for current deliveries.

A BMW i7 test vehicle featuring Solid Power cells was demonstrated in 2025. This is a late R&D / pilot-stage company — not a commercial GWh-scale cell manufacturer yet. 2026 investment expected near $100M.

companies.notes: LG Energy Solution's $5.5B standalone battery manufacturing complex in Queen Creek, AZ. Phase 1: 36 GWh cylindrical EV battery plant, construction underway, expected to complete 2026 with production starting 2026. Phase 2: 17 GWh LFP ESS pouch plant — placed on hold while LGES focuses resources on Phase 1. Total planned capacity: 53 GWh. KORE Power's 12 GWh project (originally also Queen Creek/Buckeye area) was cancelled in January 2025.

research.summary: LG Energy Solution's $5.5B Queen Creek, Arizona complex will have a total capacity of 53 GWh (36 GWh cylindrical EV + 17 GWh LFP ESS). The cylindrical plant is nearing completion with production start targeted for 2026. The LFP ESS Phase 2 facility is on hold while LGES reallocates resources to Phase 1. A Honeywell building automation partnership was announced in May 2025. KORE Power, which had separately announced a 12 GWh plant in Buckeye (near Queen Creek), cancelled its project in January 2025.

research.summary: KORE Power cancelled its $1.25B, 12 GWh KOREPlex battery factory in Buckeye, Arizona in January 2025. The CEO and founder resigned, and the site was quietly listed for sale. The project had faced persistent funding difficulties driven by surplus Chinese battery capacity and difficulty raising capital. The site had received a $850M conditional DOE loan commitment that will not proceed.
